Oops — the NAME_FORM regex in validate.py: I wrote `r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,23}\\Z'` inside a heredoc with single-quote PYEOF, so `\\Z` stays as a literal backslash-backslash-Z in the Python source → the regex has `\\Z` meaning a literal backslash followed by... Actually in the Python string literal `r'...\\Z'` the raw string contains two backslashes then 'Z' → regex: `\\` matches a literal backslash, then `Z`?? No: in a raw string `r'\\Z'` = characters `\`,`\`,`Z` → the regex `\\Z` = escaped backslash followed by... no, `\\` is an escaped backslash in regex (matching one literal `\`), then `Z` matches literal 'Z'. So the pattern requires a trailing `\Z` — wrong.

Because I quoted the heredoc with 'PYEOF', no shell escaping occurs — so `\\Z` was written literally as two chars. Let me fix to `\Z`.

Note `re.match` with `\Z`... Python's re doesn't have `\Z` (it's `\Z` in Python 3.11? Actually Python re has `\Z` — yes, Python's `re` supports `\Z` meaning end of string ✓). So `r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,23}\Z'` ✓. Also I use `.match()` not `.fullmatch()` — with `\Z` it's equivalent ✓. Let me switch to fullmatch for clarity.

Let me fix and test.
